title: Candidate
description: An input the pipeline should look for anagrams of. One line of data/candidates.jsonl.

id.description: The input's folded letters, a colon, and the category. Stable under accents, spacing and punctuation, so 'Beyoncé' and 'beyonce' are one candidate.

input.description: The text as a person would write it.

source.description: manual: added by hand. trending: the nightly fetch. submission: a reader's submission (the issue form or Build). promotion: a reader promoted an anagram of it from a search, and the review placed it.

status.description: new: waiting for its next run. enumerated: processed under its last run; pnpm hits:requeue sends it back to new when the settings or the rubric move on. unclassified: the trending feed found it but no category could be assigned. rejected: not worth running (junk, or a person asked).

about.description: One factual sentence saying what the input is, for a reader: no opinion, never about a private person. One line, ending with a full stop. Written from Wikidata's English description, by the judge where there was none, from a submission, or by the operator with pnpm hits:describe; copied to each of the input's hits.

wikipedia.description: The input's English Wikipedia article, from Wikidata's sitelink or set by the operator; copied to each of the input's hits.

anchors.description: Words related to the input to search around when it has more results than the enumeration limit: every result of an anchor search contains that word. Lowercase letters, each a subset of the input's letters.

subjects.description: Subject slugs for the input, such as actor, airline or science-fiction-film: from Wikidata's occupation, industry and genre for trending inputs, or given by hand. Ingest copies them onto the input's hits as subject: tags.

runs.description: Each queue this candidate went through, with the enumeration settings and the rubric it was processed under, and from F0 on the model that judged it and whether the routine or a person's session did, oldest first. A candidate with no runs was processed before they were recorded, under settings s1 and rubric v1.

model.description: The model that screened and judged the queue. Recorded from F0 (2026-09-19) on.

judged_by.description: Whether the judge routine or a session a person started judged the queue. Recorded from F0 (2026-09-19) on.
